Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13
September, 2024
Author: Krishan Pahal

Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150206
Court No. - 68
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 9112 of 2024
Applicant :- Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Najam Uz Zaman Khan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
Supplementary affidavit filed today by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Najam Uz Zaman Khan, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
3.

This is the second anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 25 of 2017, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC, Police Station- Kotwali Nagar,
District- Aligarh, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: The first anticipatory bail application of the applicant was disposed of by this Court vide order dated 24.11.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 11081 of 2022.

The following order is being reproduced hereunder:-
"Heard Sri Hement Pratap Singh, Advocate holding brief of Sri R.P. Mishra, learned counsel for applicants and Sri Prakhar Sharan Srivastava, Advocate holding brief of Sri Tarun Agrawal, learned counsel for the informant as well as Smt. Ladli Pandey,
learned Additional Government Advocate for State.
The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to Case Crime No.25 of 2017, under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C., P.S. Kotwali Nagar, District Aligarh.

After arguing for some time, applicants' counsel submits that the present application for anticipatory bail may be dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file a regular bail application which may be decided keeping in view the guidelines as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another reported in 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A. has and learned counsel for the informant have no objection to the prayer of learned counsel for the applicants.

In view of the above, considering the aforesaid alternative prayer made by learned counsel for the applicants, it is directed that the applicants shall surrender before the concerned court below within six weeks from today and in case a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
For the period of six weeks from today or till the time of surrender of the applicants before the concerned court below, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants, in the above case.
With the above observations and directions, this application is disposed of."
PROSECUTION STORY:
5. Facts, in brief, giving rise to the present application are that the applicant along with co-accused persons Wasim Khan, Yaseen Khan, Yusuf Khan and Kadir Ali is stated to have come to the office of the informant Abhishek Varshney and assured him and his three brothers, namely, Anurag Varshney, Anupam Varshney and Abhinav Varshney that the land agreed to be sold to them belonged to Wasim Khan and his Company, as such, two cheques worth Rs. 7,25,000/- each numbered as 841255 and 841256, respectively of Canara Bank were given by Anurag Varshney in presence of all the named accused persons.
Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188226926/
2 6.

entities.text: Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A cheque No. 0650751 worth Rs.4,50,000/- was given by Anupam Varshney of HDFC Bank and a cheque no. 685327 worth Rs.10,00,000/- of HDFC Bank was given by Abhinav Varshney and the informant Abhishek Varshney is stated to have given cheque nos. 144918 and 144919 worth Rs.
7,25,000/- each of Canara Bank to the applicant and other co-accused persons in the presence of the named eye witnesses.
It was agreed that the document shall be prepared the same day on 12.07.2022 and the registered sale-deed shall be executed thereupon.

7. The named accused persons, Wasim Khan, Yusuf Khan, Yaseen Khan along with other witnesses had gone to the office of Sub-Registrar, Tehsil Kol, District Aligarh whereby the co-accused persons are stated to have slipped from there on the pretext of offering Namaz.
8.
The money from the said cheques issued to the applicant and co-accused persons was transferred to the account of the Company.

Subsequently, the named accused persons are stated to have refused to get the said registry executed as the Company is stated to have withdrawn their rights to execute the sale-deed, as such, the informant and his brothers have been duped by the applicant and other co-accused persons of their hard earned money.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
9. It is submitted that this is the second anticipatory bail application of the applicant as the order passed in first anticipatory bail application was not on merits, as such, the applicant is entitled to file second anticipatory bail application.
10. It is argued that the FIR is delayed by about four and half years and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
11. The co-accused persons had lodged another FIR regarding the same incident and the matter is pending investigation.
12. The applicant is neither the beneficiary nor the signatory to the sale-deed.
He is stated to be only present at the time when the said cheques were handed over to the co-accused persons by the informant and his brothers.
The applicant cannot be made an accused merely on the basis of his presence.
The essential mens rea is absent qua the applicant.
13. It is further stated that not a single penny has been credited to the account of the applicant.
The money has been credited to the account of the Company.
The account statement of the Company SCT Limited has been filed as Annexure-3 to the supplementary affidavit filed in court today.
14. It is further argued that the applicant is neither a stakeholder nor the member of Board of the Company.
He has simply been made an accused as he happens to be the neighbour of the co-accused persons.
The amount mentioned in the sale-deed is less than the amount given in consideration.
15. It is also stated that the execution of the alleged sale-deeds have been stayed by this Court vide order dated 26.10.2015 passed in Writ C Nos. 59970 of 2015, 59974 of 2015 and 59976 of 2015.

sentences.text: In Writ C Nos. 63624 of 2015 and 63597 of 2015, the proceedings have been stayed on the ground of parity of Writ C No.59976 of 2015, as such, the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Writ C Nos. 63624 of 2015 and 63597 of 2015
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
17. In support of his submissions, he has placed reliance on the judgement of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 13634 of 2023 decided on 26.02.2024 and the relevant paragraph nos. 5 & 35 of the said judgement read as under :-
"5.
It is further stated in the FIR that the informant had contested several petitions up to the Supreme Court for getting certain shops vacated by filing petitions under the Rent Control Act.
The said sale deed have been executed for a consideration of Rs.3,25,00,000,/- although the real value in the open market is much more than the amount shown in the sale deeds.
As propounded in Mohd. Ibrahim (supra), to fall under the first category of false documents, it is not sufficient that a document has to be made or executed dishonestly or fraudulently.
In the case herein, the applicant has executed the sale deed conveying it to be her's and has not misrepresented anyone.
It is also admitted fact that prior to the institution of the FIR and even the said sale deeds, there were civil suits pending before the Civil Court, Bijnor.
Thus, the exception can be drawn in favour of the applicant being a lady of 74 years of age.

It is to be noted at the time of arguments in the bail application of co-accused, the facts relating to the applicant were not argued or brought forward as she was not an applicant there."
18.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
19. The applicant has no criminal history and in case, his anticipatory bail application is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE BY LEARNED AGA :
20. It is argued that there is no provision of filing second anticipatory bail application under law.

21. The applicant had earlier filed Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No.
11081 of 2022 which was withdrawn by him on 24.11.2022 and it was prayed to pass an order in the light of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another1, whereby the applicant was granted a protection of six weeks.

sentences.text: that the applicant has not complied with the said order despite being granted a protection of six weeks and he is used to defy the orders of the Court.

22. It is further argued that the applicant had filed a petition u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 36996 of 2023 before this Court and failed as it was dismissed vide order dated 01.11.2023.
23.
The applicant did not care to surrender after the said order dated 01.11.2023 also.
The said act of the applicant tantamounts to forum shopping.

24. In support of his submissions, he has placed reliance on the judgment of Supreme Court passed in Union of India vs. Cipla Limited and Another2, whereby forum shopping has been termed as "disreputable practice".

entities.text: Union of India vs. Cipla Limited and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
25. Reliance has also been placed of paragraph 43 of the judgement passed by this Court in the case of Shivam vs. State of U.P. and Another3.
26.

entities.text: Shivam vs. State of U.P. and Another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As far as the applicant in instant bail application is concerned, he was hand in glove with the other co-accused persons and was present with them at the time of handing over the cheques to co-accused persons in pursuance of common object, as such, he has committed the said offence along with the other co-accused persons.
27. The arguments tendered at bar pertain to regular bail application and cannot be agitated u/s 438 Cr.P.C., as such, the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

CONCLUSION :
28. The judgement of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 13634 of 2023 decided on 26.02.2024 does not applies to the facts and circumstances of the instant case.
29.
The filing of second anticipatory bail application is nothing but a misuse of precious time of the Court.

The earlier counsel for the applicant had filed the Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 11081 of 2022 which he had withdrawn after arguing for sometimes and had prayed that a liberty be granted to him to file regular bail application which was to be decided keeping in view the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court passed in Satendra Kumar Antil (supra).
30.
The said act of the applicant stands deprecated.

It is onerous duty of the counsel not to act on the dictats of the litigant, but to give him proper advice and should cooperate in the court proceedings instead of stalling them by filing such frivolous applications.

31. In Satpal Singh Vs. State of Punjab4, the Supreme Court has held that the satisfaction of the court for granting protection u/s 438 CrPC is different from the one u/s 439 Cr.P.C. while considering regular bail.

entities.text: Satpal Singh Vs. State of Punjab4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In Pratibha Manchanda and another Vs. State of Haryana and another5,
Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188226926/
5 the Supreme Court has opined that the relief of anticipatory bail is aimed at safeguarding individual rights.

entities.text: Pratibha Manchanda and another Vs. State of Haryana and another5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Budh Priya Maurya @ Virendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While it serves as a crucial tool to prevent the misuse of the power of arrest and protects innocent individuals from harassment, it also presents challenges in maintaining a delicate balance between individual rights and the interests of justice.
The tight rope we must walk lies in striking a balance between safeguarding individual rights and protecting public interest.

32. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and also the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, this Court finds that the arguments tendered at bar pertain to regular bail application and cannot be agitated u/s 438 Cr.P.C.
, therefore, I do not find it a fit case for granting the anticipatory bail to the applicant.
33. In view of the above, the second anticipatory bail application of the applicant is rejected.
